clue.text: Group of people who swing both ways split down the middle?

parts.note: bisexual people are attracted to both sexes, shortened to bi
a sect is a group bound by shared beliefs

explanation.surface: A wink at a club for bisexuals that has fallen out and broken in two.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is a pun: the group of bisexuals is a bi-sect.
explanation.definitionFit: To bisect is to cut something into two equal halves, the geometry term for halving.

clue.text: Expanding operation at the front: Bush and Blair initially without balls to take on the task

indicators.note: the letters take on, or add, the next piece
without here means outside, so the two letters go outside the balls
the initials of the two leaders are their first letters

parts.note: the US president, read for his first letter
the UK prime minister, read for his first letter
balls are round, like the letter O
a task is a job

explanation.surface: Bush and Blair, lacking courage, take on a military operation at the front line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expanding operation at the front' reads like a war on two fronts; it is a breast enlargement.
explanation.definitionFit: A boob job is slang for cosmetic surgery to enlarge the breasts, at the front of the body.

clue.text: Not a good place for gay activity when youth leaves

indicators.note: Y is short for young, so the youth leaving means that letter goes out of the word

parts.note: sodomy is anal sex, here crudely taken as gay activity

explanation.surface: Somewhere unsuitable for gay goings-on once the young have gone.
explanation.definitionFit: Sodom is the biblical city destroyed by God for its wickedness, so a byword for a sinful place.

clue.text: Revolutionary environment for the hooker's blow job: US choir

indicators.note: the revolutionary forms the environment, the surroundings, for the next piece

parts.note: Che Guevara is the stock revolutionary
a prostitute's blow job is oral sex

explanation.surface: A tour of a red-light setting next to an American church choir.
explanation.definitionFit: In American usage a chorale is a choir or chorus, as well as the hymn tune it sings.

clue.text: No Oscar (distraught Imelda Staunton starts a stupor)

parts.note: No. is short for number, written N

indicators.note: someone distraught is all over the place, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the starts of the two names are their opening letters

parts.note: the actress's two names, read for their first letters

explanation.surface: Imelda Staunton, nominated for Vera Drake, misses the Oscar and is left in a daze.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket reads as a gossip-column aside about the 2005 Oscars, but it is all wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Narcosis is a state of drowsiness or unconsciousness brought on by a drug, a medical word for a stupor.

clue.text: Vice president sticks one on head of Gingrich ~ Newt kicks butt

indicators.note: sticks one on means headbutts; here the single letter is stuck in front of the next piece
in a down clue, on puts the single letter above the next piece

parts.note: a means one

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: Newt Gingrich, US politician; only his first letter is used

indicators.note: the butt, or rear end, of the name is kicked off

parts.note: Gingrich's first name, losing its last letter

explanation.surface: Private Eye mock headline: a US vice president headbutts Newt Gingrich, who hits back.
explanation.walkthrough: A, G (head of Gingrich), then NEW (Newt without its butt, the last letter).
explanation.definitionFit: Spiro Agnew was Richard Nixon's Vice President until he resigned in 1973.

clue.text: Where a model might well be seen as 'pussy', 'tramp'

definitions.text: Where a model might well be seen

parts.note: pussy is a pet name for a cat
to tramp is to walk a long way

explanation.surface: A model seen as both a pussycat and a tramp.
explanation.walkthrough: The insults look like a slur on a model, but they are a pet and a hike.
explanation.definitionFit: A catwalk is the long narrow stage that fashion models walk along at a show.

clue.text: Sting getting behind as a Mensa member?

parts.note: to smart is to sting with pain
one's behind is one's arse

explanation.surface: The singer Sting getting behind the high-IQ society as a member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sting' looks like the rock singer, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A smart-arse is a know-all, and a Mensa member is a very clever person: the question mark flags the jibe.

clue.text: Melons "fallen out of containers" could well be, for example, doubly good inside

definitions.text: Melons "fallen out of containers" could well be

indicators.note: inside means the doubled letter goes into the middle of the word for example

parts.note: say means for example, as in a fruit, say, a melon

indicators.note: doubly means the letter for good is used two times

explanation.surface: A Private Eye leer: melons spilling out of their containers would surely be sagging, but good inside.
explanation.walkthrough: Melons is a crude slang term for breasts, and the containers are a bra, which is the joke behind the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Saggy means drooping, which is what breasts out of a bra would be, the double meaning of melons.

clue.text: Weird forbearing type on crew: use him if you need a fix

definitions.text: use him if you need a fix

parts.note: odd means strange or weird
the biblical Job is the byword for patience under suffering
to man a ship is to crew it

explanation.surface: A strange, patient member of a gang who is the one to call in a fix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fix' hints at a drug dealer, but it means a repair.
explanation.definitionFit: An odd-job man is a handyman paid to do small repairs and chores around the house.

clue.text: Toad arm-wrestled — he's a killer in the ring

definitions.text: he's a killer in the ring

indicators.note: letters that are wrestled are twisted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A toad wins an arm-wrestling bout and is a ring killer.
explanation.walkthrough: The ring looks like a boxing ring after the arm-wrestling, but it is a bullring.
explanation.definitionFit: A matador is the bullfighter whose role is to kill the bull in the bullring.

clue.text: Bite all round Wendy's top and give knicker elastic a sound tweak?

definitions.text: give knicker elastic a sound tweak?

indicators.note: the first word wraps all round the next piece

parts.note: a sharp tang has bite, as in a strong flavour

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the name read only for its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone bites around Wendy's top and snaps her knicker elastic.
explanation.walkthrough: Knicker elastic is a seaside-postcard joke; it is plucked like a string here, with its sound in mind.
explanation.definitionFit: To twang is to pluck a taut string or band so that it vibrates with a ringing noise.

clue.text: Good luck getting an easy lay as a teatime treat, maybe

parts.note: jam is British slang for good luck, as in jammy
tart is slang for a promiscuous woman

explanation.surface: Wishing someone luck with a willing partner, served up as something with the tea.
explanation.walkthrough: Jammy means lucky in Britain; a jam tart is a small pastry case filled with jam.
explanation.definitionFit: A jam tart is a small sweet pastry, a classic British afternoon-tea item; 'maybe' marks it as one example.

clue.text: Law, when involved with the Yard, is stinking

indicators.note: letters involved with each other are tangled together, so they are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The law, mixed up with Scotland Yard, smells rotten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stinking' looks like corruption, but here it is the slang 'stinking rich'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stinking rich is an idiom for being extremely well off, so stinking alone stands for rich.

clue.text: You'll find them plastered all over the place in our night-time city streets

definitions.meaning: plastered reads as stuck up like posters, but it is slang for very drunk

definitions.text: all over the place in our night-time city streets
definitions.meaning: the drunks are found all over British town centres after dark, and are themselves all over the place

explanation.surface: Something like fly-posters pasted on walls across a city's streets at night.
explanation.walkthrough: Binge drinking, heavy drinking in one session, was a big British news story in 2005.
explanation.definitionFit: Binge drinkers are people who drink heavily in one go, so are plastered, meaning very drunk.

clue.text: No place for Michael Howard, an even less sensitive figure?

parts.note: numb is without feeling, so number is even more numb
ten is a figure, an even one

explanation.surface: A cruel jibe that Michael Howard is a still more unfeeling figure.
explanation.walkthrough: Number Ten Downing Street is the British PM's home; Howard, the Tory leader, lost the 2005 election. 'Number' here is said with a soft b.
explanation.definitionFit: Number Ten is the official residence of the Prime Minister, so somewhere the losing opposition leader would not live.

clue.text: See 14
Staying put in the House: elected party's without alternative

parts.note: a party that is elected is in

indicators.note: without means outside, so the parties go outside the next piece

parts.note: a do is a party, so party's gives dos, plural
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: An elected party stays in the Commons with no other choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The House' looks like the House of Commons, but it is any house.
explanation.definitionFit: Indoors means inside a building, so staying put inside the house.

clue.text: Weakened Blair flips during one broadcast …

indicators.note: one piece sits during, that is inside, the other

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
something broadcast has been aired

indicators.note: flips means turned over, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: Tony Blair was the PM, Prime Minister

explanation.surface: A weakened Tony Blair makes U-turns while one programme is on air.
explanation.walkthrough: The dots lead into the next clue, which also turns on Blair and a broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: Impaired means damaged or reduced in strength, a close synonym of weakened.

clue.text: Scumbag makes topless girl dive

indicators.note: a topless word has lost its first letter

parts.note: a lass is a girl
a dive is a seedy bar, a hole

explanation.surface: A sleazebag gets a girl to strip off and work in a seedy club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topless girl' reads as a stripper; 'dive' as a plunge.
explanation.definitionFit: Asshole is American slang for a contemptible person, a strong synonym for a scumbag.

clue.text: … signal Blair to abandon broadcast and piss around

indicators.note: Blair abandons the letters for broadcast, which are taken out of him

parts.note: taken as written
to air a programme is to broadcast it

indicators.note: around here means turned round, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: to pee is to piss

explanation.surface: Some signal tells Blair to quit the broadcast and mess about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piss around' reads as fooling about; here 'around' turns the word round.
explanation.definitionFit: A bleep is a short high electronic sound used as a signal, as from a pager or alarm.

clue.text: A woman in missionary position should be adjusting pulley beneath bishop

definitions.text: A woman in missionary position should be

indicators.note: in a down answer the jumbled letters sit beneath the bishop

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: adjusting means changing the arrangement, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Sex-manual advice about a woman under a bishop, using a pulley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Missionary position' is the face-to-face sex position, with the woman on her back.
explanation.definitionFit: Belly up means lying on one's back with the stomach upwards, as a woman does in the missionary position.

clue.text: Get your hands on woman's chest; it's sort of PC

parts.note: to palm something is to take hold of it in the hand
a top is the garment covering a woman's chest

explanation.surface: An invitation to grope, hastily excused as being politically correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'PC' wants to be politically correct, but it is a personal computer.
explanation.definitionFit: A palmtop is a small handheld computer that fits in the palm of the hand.

clue.text: Put a spin on Howard's last super balls-up about "end of Conservatives"

indicators.note: Howard's last is the final letter of the Tory leader's surname

parts.note: the name read only for its final letter

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go about the next piece
a balls-up is a mess, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

parts.note: the word read only for its last letter

explanation.surface: Spinning Michael Howard's last great mess as the end of the Tories.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Howard led the Conservatives to defeat in the 2005 election.
explanation.definitionFit: To dress something up is to present it more attractively than it deserves, which is what spin does.

clue.text: Architect's style: "act loaded to get end away"

parts.note: to do is to act

indicators.note: the word loses its end, its last letter

parts.note: loaded is slang for rich

explanation.surface: An architect's taste for a drunken act of getting one's end away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting your end away' is British slang for having sex; here the word just loses its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Doric is one of the classical orders of Greek architecture, with plain fluted columns.

clue.text: Old man's got a stiffy — "'an intrusion when you're surfing the web"

definitions.text: an intrusion when you're surfing the web

parts.note: pop is slang for an old man or father
something that is up is erect

explanation.surface: An elderly man with an erection, mid-session online.
explanation.walkthrough: The old man's stiffy implies what he is surfing for.
explanation.definitionFit: A pop-up is an unwanted browser window, usually an advert, that appears over a web page.

clue.text: Source of crude smear — not Dicky

parts.note: to oil something is to smear it with grease
dicky is British slang for weak or unwell, so not dicky is well

explanation.surface: The origin of a crude slur on someone who is not called Dicky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crude' and 'smear' suggest a rude slander, and 'Dicky' looks like a name; it is the British slang for shaky.
explanation.definitionFit: An oil well is the bored hole that brings crude, meaning unrefined petroleum, out of the ground.

clue.text: After stimulant, Mark gets to display luvvy-style feelings

indicators.note: the speck comes after the drug

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
a mote is a tiny speck, a mark

explanation.surface: An actor named Mark, high on a stimulant, puts on a theatrical show of feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: A luvvy is a gushing actor, British slang. 'Mark' looks like a name.
explanation.definitionFit: To emote is to show emotion in an exaggerated, theatrical way, typical of a hammy actor.

clue.text: Made to look old, backsliding cavorter, Hoover dropped out

indicators.note: sliding back means the remaining letters are read from end to start
the vacuum cleaner's letters, read backwards with the rest, drop out of the word

parts.note: taken as written
a Hoover is a vacuum cleaner, a vac

explanation.surface: A dancer of the past who has slid back, while a Hoover has quit.
explanation.walkthrough: Hoover is a brand that stands for any vacuum cleaner in Britain, shortened here to vac.
explanation.definitionFit: Retro describes a modern thing styled to imitate the fashions of an earlier era.

clue.text: Adopt cautious approach to women, sexually — then paw

parts.note: pussy is crude slang for women seen sexually
an animal's foot is its paw

explanation.surface: Someone advised to take care with women, and then to grope them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paw' looks like groping, but it is just a foot.
explanation.definitionFit: To pussyfoot is to act timidly and avoid committing oneself, treading as softly as a cat.

clue.text: Conservative to try "disregard of rule of law"

parts.note: taken as an abbreviation for a Conservative
to tempt is an old sense of to test or try, as in tempting fate

explanation.surface: A Tory sets out to try 'flouting the law' as a slogan.
explanation.definitionFit: Contempt of court is wilful disobedience or disrespect towards a court, a legal breach of its authority.

clue.text: Maintenance makes you puke — put that on the record

indicators.note: makes is read as remakes, so the following word is reworked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Household upkeep is so dull it makes you sick, and that should be put on record.
explanation.definitionFit: Upkeep is the cost or work of keeping something in good repair, the same as its maintenance.
